_rule: <Name> — <what it is> for <when to use it>. Plain words, no jargon, <= 90 characters, no commas.
_why: The line IS the name, because asset.name is the only per-asset free text a motion graphic has and the only text at all an audio asset has. One definition; if a description field turns out to be read, the same bytes go there.
_separator_note: The twelve components and seven caption styles use an EM DASH. The thirteen sounds already shipped with a HYPHEN in their filenames. Both parse; changing the sounds means thirteen re-uploads. Flagged for Zac rather than normalised silently.
components: PlainText — a bold line over the picture for one claim you want read
CaptionMatch — a line styled like the captions for a beat that should read as spoken
LowerThird — a name above a role for introducing the person on screen
QuoteCard — a serif quote with a name under it for a line worth quoting
TornPaper — two slammed strips of text for a two-beat punchline
StickyNotes — three handwritten notes for three short takeaways
EmojiCard — a big emoji with a caption under it for a reaction beat
StatCard — a big number that counts up for a figure worth landing
Stamp — a red distressed stamp struck across the frame for a verdict
PillCluster — a row of small labelled pills for a set of attributes
RankedList — numbered rows with time badges for steps or a ranking
Reticle — green targeting brackets with a scan line for pointing at something
caption_styles: CleanCut — plain white words for when the words should not draw attention
Cove — words in a soft rounded box for keeping text readable over a busy shot
Gadzhi — one keyword lit in colour for making the key word land
Lumen — a bright band behind the line for a loud high-energy beat
Prime — two stacked lines for when a sentence needs room to breathe
Pulse — the whole line fades in for a calm even delivery
TwoTone — every word outlined in a second colour for a punchy look
sounds: boom - deep low impact for a heavy landing
punchsfx - sharp hit for a hard word
popsfx - short pop for a graphic appearing
camera-flash - short bright shutter click for a snap or a cut
woosh-professional - cleaner whoosh for a polished move
transition-sfx - whoosh for a scene change
iphoneding - notification chime for a message beat
money-ching - cash register for a money figure
mouse-click-sound - one click for a UI action
wompwomp - sad trombone for a failure beat
rizz - rising flourish for a flirty or smug beat
